data.narrative:
Zoo is a seed-stage robotics and manufacturing company founded by Jessie Frazelle, Jordan Noone, Jenna Bryant, and Hannah Bollar, having raised $35.5M to date. The robotics and manufacturing sector includes 9 private peers and 1 public comparable, though the narrow seed-stage peer universe is constrained—only 1 same-stage datapoint exists within the sector, preventing reliable peer-median triangulation.

Given data limitations, stage-progression methodology is the primary applicable approach. Using total raised ($36M) as a valuation proxy and applying a 2.5x step-up multiplier typical of seed-to-next-stage advancement yields an implied valuation of $89M. This method directly reflects Zoo's capital deployment and stage position relative to typical progression patterns in frontier tech.

The triangulated analysis supports a valuation range of $75M to $102M, with a median point of $89M. The range derives from reasonable variance around the stage-progression result; the lower bound applies conservative step-up assumptions while the upper bound reflects higher-end market conditions. The single-method foundation introduces meaningful uncertainty. Refinement would require either comparable company multiples from a sufficiently large peer cohort or revenue/unit economics data to support revenue-based methodologies. Until such data materializes, this range should be treated as indicative rather than definitive.
